title: Fibre and image dimension bounds for finite-type schemes over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. All dimensions are topological Krull dimensions, with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then
$$\dim\overline{f(X)}\leq\dim X.$$
Moreover, if $d,n\geq0$ are integers, $\dim Y\leq d$, and every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has dimension at most $n$, then
$$\dim X\leq d+n.$$
The closure in the first inequality is the topological closure in $Y$, and no dominance, properness, flatness, irreducibility or algebraic-closedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, lemma-dimension-fibres-locally-algebraic, (2)(a) and its proof, applied to finitely many irreducible components; dim X - dim closure f(X) is the generic-fibre transcendence degree.

proof.text: Finite type over the Noetherian field gives a Noetherian source X and a locally Noetherian target Y. The over-morphism identity identifies f followed by the structure map of Y with the structure map of X. The local finite-type cancellation theorem therefore makes f locally of finite type.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, image-point transcendence-degree argument; finite generic-point cover and specialization-chain dimension comparison

proof.text: There are finitely many irreducible components of X, each with a generic point because schemes are sober. Thus there is a finite set G of points whose specializations cover X (the existing theorem IsClosed.exists_finite_forall_exists_specializes). The finite union of the closures of f(G) is closed. Continuity sends every specialization of a point of G to a specialization of its image, so this closed union contains f(X), and therefore its closure.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, image-point transcendence-degree argument; finite generic-point cover and specialization-chain dimension comparison

proof.text: For every point x of G, the proved image-point closure inequality bounds dim closure {f(x)} by dim closure {x}, and subspace monotonicity bounds the latter by dim X. A closed subset covered by closures of points whose dimensions are bounded by N has dimension at most N: order points by specialization, use the height bound at each point and then take the supremum of heights. Apply the existing theorem topologicalKrullDim_le_of_subset_iUnion_closure_singleton with N=dim X to the closed cover just obtained. This proves the first clause, including an empty source.

source.place: Tag 0B2L, image-point transcendence-degree argument; finite generic-point cover and specialization-chain dimension comparison

proof.text: The fibre homeomorphism f.fiberHomeo y identifies the scheme-theoretic fibre with the topological fibre, so the given bound n bounds every topological fibre. Apply the existing source-dimension bound to f, giving dim X at most dim Y+n. Addition is monotone, so dim Y at most d implies dim X at most d+n. Naturals embed additively into WithBot ENat. This also includes empty schemes.

lean.statement: theorem Scheme.Hom.finiteType_fibre_image_dimension_bounds {k : Type u} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] : topologicalKrullDim (closure (Set.range f)) ≤ topologicalKrullDim X ∧ ∀ (d n : ℕ), topologicalKrullDim Y ≤ (d : WithBot ℕ∞) → (∀ y : Y, topologicalKrullDim (f.fiber y) ≤ (n : WithBot ℕ∞)) → topologicalKrullDim X ≤ ((d + n : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
